text:
maya: heads up — APAC hosted demand spiked overnight, we're seeing a reserved capacity shortfall in singapore region. alert from ops-bot attached below. can we sketch a quick mitigation?

ops-bot: [ALERT] 2025-11-12T02:03:20Z reserved-utilization > 95% in ap-southeast1 for gpu-pool-hosted, fallback routing triggered 372 times in the last 1h 

liam: ugh. what's the committed vs observed numbers?

maya: short summary: committed = 240 A100-equivalent GPUs (pooled across regions), observed peak concurrently used by hosted = ~312 A100-equivalent in last 2h. effective shortfall ~72 GPUs (~30%). that's across ap-southeast1 + ap-northeast1 hotspots.

harper: did billing show any surprise Zonal reservations or SKU mapping changes? last week's invoice had a slightly different SKU mapping for the new family. @shreya can you check? :eyes:

shreya: looking now. preliminary: billing invoice included a one-off adjustment in us-central that bumped committed-cost allocation to apac incorrectly. filing with cloud billing support.

nate: short-term ops idea: enable cross-region fallback to eu-west1 for non-latency-sensitive hosted jobs and carve a 20% emergency transient pool from existing reserved capacity. could reduce immediate tail pressure.

liam: math check: if we carve 20% of 240 -> 48 GPUs transient, that still leaves 24 GPU shortfall. we need ~72. so we'll need additional spot/ephemeral capacity to make up the rest.

maya: proposal: multiplex-reserve split: keep 75% of commitments as steady (180 GPUs), 15% as burst buffer (36 GPUs, zonal sticky), and allow 10% to be flex (use spot or on-demand when needed). pair with prefix caching + token-buckets to reduce e2e demand while we flip routing.

harper: ok but legal/SLAs: we promised <200ms P95 for standard tier in apac. routing to eu-west1 will break that for some customers. need a targeted list: which customers are latency-sensitive?

liam: we can use per-customer model routing policy — fallback only for non-SLA tenants. quick query: 
```
SELECT tenant_id, tier, avg_p95_latency_apac
FROM telemetry.same_window(\'2025-11-12T01:00:00Z\', \"2025-11-12T03:00:00Z\")
WHERE avg_requests_per_min > 10
ORDER BY avg_p95_latency_apac DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

maya: thanks. @ops-bot can you run the above and dump to /tmp/apac_latency_top200.csv ?

ops-bot: running query, ETA ~ 40s.

ops-bot: done. /tmp/apac_latency_top200.csv (checksum: 6a7f2c)

shreya: billing update: cloud support found invoice mapping bug — committed credits were tagged to wrong project id for a subset of apac reservations. net effect: we *do* have the capacity committed in the account, but internal mapping made them invisible to the allocation engine. filing internal ticket to correct allocation metadata.

nate: that explains why the control plane thought we were short even though commitments exist. can we hot-fix allocator to trust cross-account reservations if tag mismatch heuristics match?

liam: yes, temporary patch: allocator should reconcile using attachment IDs instead of project tag, and fallback to 'last-known-attachment' if tag missing. simple flag: `--allocator-trust-attachment-id=true`. We should gate this behind a canary.

maya: action items:
- shreya: escalate billing fix with cloud and confirm when reservations show as allocated (ETA 4h)
- liam: prepare allocator patch + canary plan (ETA 2h)
- nate: wire transient spot pool + routing policy for non-SLA tenants (ETA 1.5h)
- harper: compile list of latency-sensitive customers and acceptable fallback policies (ETA 45m)

harper: will do. adding PRD link: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/reserve-fallback

shreya: cloud support responded — they will remap SKUs within 3 business days, but provided a short-term reconciliation API that returns actual attached reservations. requesting API token now.

liam: will open a tiny PR to toggle the allocator flag and add a metric `allocator.reservation_mismatch_reconciled` to monitor. canary in eu-west1 first.

nate: configuring a new ephemeral pool: `pool: apac-emergency-spot`, autoscale target 150-400% based on accel-queue depth. will create safety limit to avoid cost blowout.

maya: finance check — if we lean on spots + temporary on-demand for ~72 GPUs for 24-48h what cost hit are we looking at? @finance-bot / @shreya pls approximate.

finance-bot: estimated delta: spot avg hourly = $1.10 / GPU-hr, on-demand = $3.40 / GPU-hr. 72 GPUs * 24h * spot = ~$1,900/day. If on-demand used for same period = ~$5,900/day. Recommend prefer spot + throttling.

shreya: noted. also if cloud remap is fast we avoid recurring extra. will push ticket to priority P0.

maya: moving to execute — liam, nate, harper: coordinate in the next hour. i’ll post status updates every 30m. :rocket:

harper: brief status update 30m: allocator PR opened (link: https://redwood.internal/pr/3456), canary target eu-west1, monitoring dashboards updated.

liam: canary metrics look good after patch: `reservation_mismatch_reconciled` jumped from 0 to 42 in eu-west1, latency unchanged for canary tenants. rolling to apac-staging now.

ops-bot: routing rule applied: non-sla-fallback -> eu-west1. impacted fallback count dropped 60%.

maya: final note: billing remap still pending but reconciler + spot buffer bought us enough runway ~36h. we'll reconvene after cloud confirms remap or by end of day. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

harper: closing loop later — filing postmortem template in #postmortems once we have exact timelines.

nate: leaving a short snippet for runbook updates: 
```
- symptom: allocator reports reservation shortfall but billing shows commitments active
- quickfix: enable --allocator-trust-attachment-id=true and reconcile
- mitigation: create apac-emergency-spot pool + non-sla-fallback routing
- long term: fix billing tag pipeline and add reservation-mapping healthcheck
```

maya: good. end thread for now.
